items.title: Live: Tempers flare as England and Argentina play spiteful World Cup semifinal
items.description: England and Argentina rekindle one of the World Cup's most heated rivalries when they meet in the semifinal in Atlanta, with Spain awaiting the winner. Follow live.

items.title: Albanese rolls out a rule book and a red carpet for AI companies
items.description: If Australia is truly going to coax major AI companies to choose us rather than the other suitor nations with similar ambitions, some tough decisions need to be made soon.

items.title: Artists seek 'seat at table' in AI office
items.description: The creative sector hopes there is a space to contribute to the Office of AI, given its content powers a lot of these tools.

items.title: Q-Day is coming, and it might break the entire internet
items.description: The countdown is on to Q-Day, when an algorithm written more than 30 years ago could run on a quantum computer and compromise the security of data on the internet. How are we preparing?

items.title: Gender quota debate revived in Liberals' soul-searching mission
items.description: Liberal Party HQ has admitted it is "in the political fight of our lives" as it canvasses ideas, including reviving gender quotas, to take the party forward.

items.title: US launches strikes on key Iranian island amid renewed threats
items.description: US Central Command said it launched a 90-minute attack targeting Iran's strategic Greater Tunb Island.

items.title: Trump's tariffs turn liability as businesses claw back $110 billion
items.description: Businesses globally are clawing back tens of billions of dollars paid to United States customs after Donald Trump's so-called liberation day tariffs were deemed unlawful.

items.title: Why Australians shouldn't panic about fuel prices as war in Iran escalates again
items.description: With the price of oil rising and the fuel excise cut due to end, drivers are facing twin threats when it comes to the price of fuel, but experts say Australia is in a much better position compared with when the Middle East conflict began.

items.title: Global reserves that spared the worst of the oil shock are spent, IMF says
items.description: The International Monetary Fund says the global economy was spared the worst of the oil price shock because of large reserves. Now they are running out.

items.title: Telstra and telco regulator prepare for grilling over widespread outage
items.description: Telstra prepares for a grilling in parliament about the recent network outage that disrupted Australia, with the communications regulator also set to face tough questions.

items.title: NDIS 'failing' some of the very people it was set up to protect
items.description: Experts say the National Disability Insurance Scheme is failing people like Lucy, whose one-on-one care for severe disability has been deemed "not value for money".

items.title: University leader says her sector is 'most prominent' for rising antisemitism
items.description: Professor Jennifer Westacott, the chancellor of Western Sydney University, says tertiary institutions have hidden behind freedom of expression to avoid taking action on hate speech.

items.title: Electoral boundary shakeup leaves politicians with a big decision
items.description: Some notable politicians are among the 114,000 Tasmanians displaced by electoral boundary changes, and now have a difficult decision to make — stick with the electorate that voted them in, or move with the communities they've long been aligned with and live in.

items.title: The Odyssey may be the epic we deserve, but not the one we need
items.description: The scope of Christopher Nolan's latest epic might be awesome but a menagerie of supporting faces and questionable characterisations muddle the director's vision.

items.title: I tried to use voodoo to win a TV show, and in some ways it worked
items.description: Halfway through the Race Around The World competition, I'm second last on the leaderboard. So, I decide to cheat.

items.title: From Mozart to the Beatles, prove you're a music genius with this quiz
items.description: From famous icons and musical terms to unusual instruments and classical influences in popular music, test your knowledge with this quiz.

items.title: Disgraced footballer Nicky Winmar removed from AFL Hall of Fame
items.description: Winmar was found guilty earlier this month of three counts of unlawful assault and common law assault.

items.title: An alias and a dead man's name: Former ATO executive charged with fraud
items.description: Former assistant tax commissioner Nick Petroulias has been charged with multiple fraud offences, accused of obtaining financial advantage by deception and using false documents.

items.title: Victim of violent robbery describes attackers as 'pure evil'
items.description: The 76-year-old victim of a violent robbery on Tasmania's east coast has described the people who attacked him as "pure evil".

items.title: Moira Deeming drops court bid against party after last-ditch plea to retain candidacy
items.description: Victorian MP Moira Deeming faces being disendorsed as a Liberal candidate for refusing to apologise to former party leader Matthew Guy, after accusing him of assaulting her at a community event in May.

items.title: GP clinic network hit by major cyber breach
items.description: Partnered Health, which operates more than 50 general practice and skin cancer clinics across Australia, has identified more than a dozen clinics where it fears patient information was taken.

items.title: Employees sue Meta over claims AI systems selected workers for lay-offs
items.description: Many of the employees in the lawsuit took pregnancy or parental leave, during which time they would not have worked and thus had their measured output reduced.

items.title: Government moves on AI data centres and copyright
items.description: The prime minister has unveiled Labor's plan for new AI national standards, warning Australia has a narrow window to set AI's "social licence". A new set of standards for artificial intelligence will provide clear rules for data centres, forcing them to minimise water usage and underwrite or supply their own power. Anthony Albanese has vowed AI companies will not be able to use Australian books, music, art or news to train AI "without the artist's control".

items.title: School worker on child abuse material charges denied bail
items.description: The 35-year-old woman, who is seven months' pregnant, is in custody after police discovered alleged child abuse material on her mobile phone.

items.title: Trump reverses temporary pause on traffic stops after recent fatal shootings
items.description: US President Donald Trump says federal immigration agents will continue carrying out vehicle stops, reversing a temporary pause announced by officials just a day earlier.
